Neonatal dexamethasone has been reported to improve pulmonary outcome and assist weaning from mechanical ventilation in infants that have developed bron- chopulmonary dysplasia. Dexamethasone is also one of the drugs of choice for the man- agement of severe croup (see p.1502). However, as with other corticosteroids (p.1500) it appears to be of little value in bronchi- olitis.1,2 1. Roosevelt G, et al. Dexamethasone in bronchiolitis: a ran- domised controlled trial. Lancet 1996; 348: 292–5. 2. Klassen TP, et al. Dexamethasone in salbutamol-treated inpa- tients with acute bronchiolitis: a randomized controlled trial. J Pediatr 1997; 130: 191–6. For mention of the uncertain ef- fect of neonatal dexamethasone on retinopathy of prematurity, see Effects on the Neonate, under Adverse Effects above.
